LW
By Lisa Warren · Founder & CEO, Neural Horizons AI

Let me clear something up before you press play, because if I don't, the title will do all the work for me and none of it correctly. The AI Death Spiral is not a story about AI dying. AI is not the villain. AI is the way out.

It's the story of companies that had every chance to use it, and quietly refused it. One meeting, one deferred pilot, one "we'll look at training next year" at a time. That refusal has a shape, and the shape has a name.

I've spent two years sitting across tables from leadership teams that fit the pattern exactly. Same shape every time. Same ending every time. In this preview episode of The Agentic, I walk through it start to finish — in about the time it takes to make a coffee.

What you'll hear · 11 minThe whole map, out loud

The six signatures The three mechanics The UAE 24-month clock The five-step rescue

The six signatures I keep filing. The spreadsheet fiefdom. The system nobody describes. The weekly manual compile. The pilot that never starts. The "we're not ready" reflex. And the silent one — the skilling freeze.

The three mechanics behind every refusal. None of them technical. The mirror is the threat. The trust maths — no trust, no upskilling, no capability, more reason to refuse. And the political ledger, where the "no" is never written down, which is why it can never be answered.

The clock. On 4 May 2026 Dubai gave its private sector 24 months to go agentic. The UAE Cabinet committed to 50% of federal services on autonomous agents by 2028. Deloitte: 74% of companies plan agentic AI, 21% have the governance for it. That gap is where the market splits.

The tool works. The will does not. And the clock is running whether the boardroom looks at it or not.

The exit · 5 boring stepsThe rescue, in order

None of this is a corporate renaissance. It's five decisions, all of them unglamorous, all of them available today:

The whole thing on one page

  1. One accountable owner. Not a rotating point of contact.
  2. The mandate in writing. One line signed by the CEO — this is a company initiative, not an IT side project.
  3. A read-only mirror. AI that reads every system and physically cannot touch a transaction. Fear drops the moment nothing can go wrong.
  4. One boring pilot. 90 days, on the most contained function you have. The winning pilot is always the least impressive candidate.
  5. One success metric. One go / no-go. Then — and only then — the next wave.
AI isn't here to take your job. AI is here to take your spreadsheet — and your "we'll see."

The role you're protecting at the all-hands is costing you the company one quarter at a time. Bring the tool in the way you'd bring the auditors in — with a mandate, a deadline, and a named owner. That is the exit. It's been in the room the whole time.
